NetSimR

NetSimR is an R package of actuarial functions for non-life insurance and reinsurance pricing, reserving and capital modelling, with six Shiny tools for simulating claims, fitting distributions and GLMs, reserving, pricing excess of loss reinsurance and the capital of a portfolio. Its website, with every help page and the vignettes, is https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/, where the tools can also be tried in the browser, with nothing to install.

Installation 

# the released version from CRAN
install.packages("NetSimR")

# the development version from GitHub
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("NetSimAnalytics/NetSimR")

What it does

  • Capped means, exposure curves and increased limit factors (ILFs) for LogNormal, Gamma, Pareto, sliced LogNormal-Pareto and sliced Gamma-Pareto claim sizes.
  • Sliced distributions: mean, density, cdf and quantile function of the sliced LogNormal-Pareto and Gamma-Pareto distributions.
  • Pure IBNR exposure from a LogNormal or Gamma reporting delay.
  • Claims simulation with a frequency-severity model, Pareto tail slices, a severity cap, each-and-every-loss layers with reinstatements and their premiums, aggregate layers, and each period’s largest claim (OEP), run in parallel when that is faster; portfolios of several lines joined by a Gaussian or t copula, with VaR, TVaR, diversification and capital allocation.
  • Claims reserving: the chain ladder with Mack’s standard errors and tail factors, Bornhuetter-Ferguson, Benktander and Cape Cod, a bootstrap of the reserves’ distribution, the one-year view (Merz-Wuthrich), the Munich chain ladder of paid and incurred claims, Clark’s growth curves, a chain ladder for claims inflation, and actual against expected development.
  • Pricing models: a Tweedie family for GLMs of the loss cost.
  • Excess of loss pricing: the burning cost with indexation, development and aggregate terms, a Pareto model of the large losses, exposure rating with the Swiss Re and Lloyd’s (MBBEFD) curves or a claim size distribution, credibility blending and the technical premium with reinstatements.
  • Six Shiny tools: a claims simulator with reports and run comparison; a distribution fitting tool for claim counts and sizes, including claims reported only above a threshold or capped at policy limits, with Q-Q plots and Anderson-Darling tests, whose fits it saves as simulator settings; a GLM fitting tool with a Tweedie family, splines and bands, variable selection (stepwise, lasso, elastic net, ridge), validation on held-out rows (Gini, lift and double lift), a rate table and scoring of new data; a reserving tool with a report; a reinsurance pricing tool; and a portfolio capital tool with copulas and capital allocation.

Examples 

library(NetSimR)

# mean claim size capped at 600 for a Pareto with scale 200 and shape 1.2
# (the older CamelCase names, such as ParetoCappedMean(), still work)
pareto_capped_mean(600, 200, 1.2)

# increased limit factor from 700 to 1,000 for Gamma claim sizes
ilf_gamma(700, 1000, 1, 0.0005)

# Gamma body sliced at 3,000 with a Pareto tail of shape 1.4
psliced_gamma_pareto(5000, 1.2, 0.0004, 3000, 1.4)

# pure IBNR exposure (in days) of three periods, with a Gamma reporting delay
pure_ibnr_gamma(
  as.Date(c("2006-01-01", "2006-07-01", "2007-01-01")),
  as.Date(c("2006-12-31", "2007-06-30", "2007-12-31")),
  as.Date("2007-10-30"),
  shape = 7, rate = 0.15
)

# 10,000 years of Poisson claim counts with LogNormal claim sizes, a Pareto tail
# above 100,000, and a layer of 50,000 excess of 20,000 on each claim with two
# reinstatements at 100% of an upfront premium of 10,000
ceded <- simulate_claims(
  10000, "Poisson", 3, "LogNormal", c(meanlog = 8, sdlog = 1.5), seed = 1,
  pareto_thresholds = 100000, pareto_alphas = 1.5,
  eel_layer = "limited", eel_deductible = 20000, eel_limit = 50000,
  eel_reinstatements = 2, eel_premium = 10000
)
mean(ceded$total_claims)
mean(ceded$reinstatement_premium)

# chain ladder reserves of the RAA triangle with Mack's standard errors and a
# fitted tail, then the 99.5th percentile of the bootstrapped total reserve
chain_ladder(raa_triangle, tail = "exponential")
bootstrap_chain_ladder(raa_triangle, n = 10000, seed = 1)$total[["p99.5"]]

# the one-year view of the same reserves, and paid and incurred claims projected together
merz_wuthrich(raa_triangle)$total
munich_chain_ladder(quarg_mack_paid, quarg_mack_incurred)$total

# a layer of 4m excess of 1m priced on its experience and on a property risk
# profile with the Swiss Re Y3 exposure curve
burning_cost(xl_large_losses, xl_premium[, c("year", "premium")], 1e6, 4e6,
             inflation = 0.04, rating_premium = 60e6)
property_exposure_rating(xl_property_profile, 1e6, 4e6, curve = "Y3", loss_ratio = 0.55)

Shiny tools 

run_shiny_simulator()                  # claims simulator
run_shiny_distribution_fitting_tool()  # frequency and severity fits
run_shiny_glm_fitting_tool()           # generalised linear models
run_shiny_reserving_tool()             # claims reserving
run_shiny_reinsurance_pricing_tool()   # excess of loss pricing
run_shiny_portfolio_tool()             # portfolio capital

Problems and ideas are welcome as GitHub issues; each tool’s About card links to them.

Vignettes

Seven vignettes set out the theory behind the functions and work through examples:

  • From pricing to capital and reserves: a motor portfolio, which follows one portfolio through the package
  • Capped means, exposure curves and increased limit factors
  • Sliced LogNormal-Pareto and Gamma-Pareto distributions
  • Pure IBNR exposure from a reporting delay distribution
  • Simulating claims with simulate_claims()
  • Claims reserving with the chain ladder and its relatives
  • Pricing an excess of loss layer

They are on the package’s CRAN page, and browseVignettes("NetSimR") opens the copies installed with the package (a development version installed from GitHub has them only when installed with build_vignettes = TRUE).

References

The methods are described in articles by Yiannis Parizas in The Actuary: Free for All (2023), Escaping the triangle (2019) and Taken to excess (2019).

How to cite

If NetSimR helps your work, please cite it; citation("NetSimR") gives the reference for the version installed, and a BibTeX entry:

Parizas, Y. (2026). NetSimR: Actuarial Functions for Non-Life Insurance Modelling. R package version 0.4.0. https://netsimanalytics.github.io/NetSimR/

A star on GitHub or a mention to a colleague also helps others find it.
